correctness.rationale: The proof checks arbitrary centered ellipsoids, not only Euclidean or diagonal ones. Averaging signed clique inequalities gives the diagonal vector \(s\in P_G\); a stable-set convex decomposition of \(s\) forces a reciprocal weight at least \(d\); averaging signed stable-set points in the inverse quadratic form and using \(q_{ii}(Q^{-1})_{ii}\ge1\) gives \(\lambda^2\ge d\). The standard symmetric John theorem gives the reverse inequality. All quantifiers include \(d=1\), and the finite exact-rational replay independently checks 1087 perfect graphs through five vertices with two nontrivial ellipsoid families.

The inspected modern equality-case source supplies the general distance bound but neither the unconditional-reflexive class nor the reciprocal stable-set argument. The accepted statement therefore does not follow from either inspected source alone; its key step is the new conversion of arbitrary ellipsoid diagonal data into a stable-set convex decomposition.
residual_risks: An obscure or poorly indexed Banach-space source could conceivably contain the same synthesis. The inspected foundational and current equality-case literature do not state it, and targeted equivalent-formulation searches found no covering result.

The theorem is mathematically implied by the new reciprocal-weight argument together with standard published ingredients; originality is claimed for this exact class-wide statement and proof, not for the individual ingredients.

value.rationale: The result identifies an entire combinatorially classified lattice-polytope class as equality bodies for the universal symmetric John bound, rather than computing an ad hoc example. It converts perfect-graph structure into a sharp affine-geometric extremality statement and immediately covers structured families such as signed Birkhoff polytopes. The invariant is canonical, affine, and central in convex geometry; the conclusion is exact in every dimension.
